solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Remove restaurant retrospectively charging uncapped fee

indicators.note: charging in the sense of loading, so the uncapped fee is filled with the next part
uncapped means the word loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a caff is British slang for a cheap cafe or restaurant

explanation.surface: A diner returns to a restaurant that charged a fee without the usual cap.
explanation.walkthrough: The restaurant is a caff, British slang for a cheap cafe; 'charging' means loading, not billing.
explanation.definitionFit: To efface is to wipe out or erase, which is to remove a mark or memory.

clue.text: Fine old cat hiding tail in folded paper

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: hiding tail means the word's last letter is hidden away

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A fine old cat hides its tail in a folded sheet of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a sheet of paper folded once to make two leaves of a book.

clue.text: Discrimination distorted hit parade

indicators.note: something distorted is twisted out of its proper shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the pop charts are skewed and unfair to some artists.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was South Africa's system of racial segregation, the most notorious example of institutional discrimination.

clue.text: 'Throw up' (to quote author) with this medicine

indicators.note: in a down entry, throwing something up sends its letters upwards, so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cite is to quote
the author of a clue refers to the setter, ME

explanation.surface: An author quoted saying 'throw up', as if describing what a certain medicine makes you do.
explanation.walkthrough: CITE ME, read upwards, gives the answer; the quoted 'Throw up' doubles as a nod to what the medicine does.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a medicine or substance taken to induce vomiting.

clue.text: Cut back relations with company controlling international minister?

indicators.note: going back means the word for cut is written from right to left

parts.note: CO (company) with I (international) placed in front, as if the firm is the power behind the international
IT is slang for sexual relations
to lop is to cut; read backwards

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a minister who severed ties with a company running an international business.
explanation.walkthrough: The positioning of I before CO is loose: 'controlling' just links the two abbreviations rather than putting one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A politico is a politician, and a government minister is one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Jockey mostly prefers congenial fast mover

indicators.note: to jockey is to jostle for position, so the letters jostle into a new order
mostly means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A rider mostly likes a friendly racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jockey' looks like the subject of the sentence; it is the anagram signal, a verb meaning to jostle.
explanation.definitionFit: The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal on earth, diving at over 300 km/h.

clue.text: Attractive characteristic of The Third Man elevating the finale

parts.note: like means typical or characteristic of, as in just like him

indicators.note: in a down answer, elevating the finale lifts the last letter above the one before it, swapping the final pair

parts.note: Abel was the third man in Genesis, after Adam and Cain

explanation.surface: A film buff admires a trait of The Third Man, its famous ending.
explanation.walkthrough: The Third Man is a 1949 film, but here it is the third man in the Bible, after Adam and Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: Likeable means pleasant and easy to warm to, so attractive in personality.

clue.text: Code for the Speaker's tea dance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the NATO alphabet code word for T, which is how tea is spoken
second meaning: the Argentine ballroom dance

explanation.surface: The Commons Speaker's rules for afternoon tea dances.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic description: the word tea pronounced is the letter T, whose NATO phonetic code word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a passionate ballroom dance from Argentina, and Tango is the radio code word for T.

clue.text: Alsace beer brewed without English vegetable

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so the letters are stirred into a new order
without means the following abbreviation is taken out of the mixture

parts.note: the letters to mix
E is the abbreviation for English; one E is removed

explanation.surface: A beer made in Alsace that leaves out English hops or produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Calabrese is a variety of green broccoli, a familiar vegetable.

clue.text: Divide prime bit of Camembert the French way

indicators.note: the prime or first part of the cheese's name is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter
le is French for the
Ave is the abbreviation for avenue, a way

explanation.surface: Cutting the best wedge of Camembert in the French manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleave is to split or divide something, typically with a sharp blow.

clue.text: Family haunting retired senior cause further provocation

indicators.note: haunting means the family word lingers inside the next piece
retired means drawn back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: an elder is a senior person
kin are family

explanation.surface: Relatives keep haunting a retired old man and cause more trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' does double duty in the surface as pensioned off; in the wordplay it means drawn back, so read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To rekindle a quarrel is to stir it up again, provoking anger once more.

clue.text: Trivial affair keeping Wellington away from the front?

indicators.note: keeping means the affair word holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a fling is a short love affair

indicators.note: away from the front means the first letter is lost

parts.note: a wellington is a rubber boot

explanation.surface: A light romance keeps the Duke of Wellington from the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellington looks like the general; it is a wellington boot, which loses its B.
explanation.definitionFit: Footling means petty and unimportant, a dismissive word for something trifling.

clue.text: Graduates going head to head about shell of obscure creature

indicators.note: about means the graduates go around the next piece

parts.note: MA and BA are both degrees for graduates; the MA is turned to face the BA, so the two front letters meet

indicators.note: the shell of a word is its outside letters

parts.note: its first and last letters give OE

explanation.surface: Two graduates argue face to face about the shell of some obscure creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The graduates are the master's and bachelor's degrees; 'head to head' turns the first round so the two front letters meet.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism, a microscopic creature that changes shape as it moves.

clue.text: Player from Expresso Bongo extremely withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the chosen letters are read in reverse
at the extremes means only the outermost letters of each word are used

parts.note: the outside letters
the outside letters

explanation.surface: A musician from the 1959 Cliff Richard film Expresso Bongo becomes a recluse.
explanation.walkthrough: Expresso Bongo was a 1959 British musical film starring Cliff Richard.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is an instrument that is played, and in an orchestra the word can stand for its player too.

clue.text: Site of massive gathering from which there's no escape

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a huge crowd at an event, or a prison camp
setter's reading: a region of space where enormous mass collects and even light cannot get out

explanation.walkthrough: Massive suggests a huge crowd; read literally it means having great mass, as astronomers use it.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy, it is a collapsed star whose gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can leave it.

clue.text: Inappropriate clue for 'demit'? It's just a reversal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: coming at the wrong moment, unsuitable

definitions.text: clue for 'demit'? It's just a reversal
definitions.meaning: second meaning, a cryptic one: read as a clue, the answer means 'timed, badly arranged', and those five letters are only demit written backwards

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a clue, the answer means 'timed, badly arranged', which gives DEMIT; since TIMED is simply DEMIT backwards, it would be a lazy clue, which is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-timed means coming at an unsuitable moment, so it describes something inopportune or out of place.

clue.text: Start to interpret three notes about quarantine

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter
so, la and ti, three notes of the sol-fa scale
on means about, as in a talk on a topic

explanation.surface: A musician starts to interpret a three-note motif about being locked down.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarantine is the enforced separation of people or animals to stop disease spreading, a form of isolation.

clue.text: Naked lovers' rampant favourites go too far

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its outer letters, leaving the middle
rampant means rearing up, so in this down answer the word is read upwards

parts.note: pets are favourites

explanation.surface: Naked lovers run wild with their favourites and go too far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rampant' looks like wild behaviour, but in heraldry it means rearing up, which in a down answer turns the word upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstep is to cross a limit, behaving beyond what is acceptable.

clue.text: Read rude review inwardly showing spirit

indicators.note: inwardly means taking only the inner letters of each word, discarding the outer ones

parts.note: the inner letters
the inner letters
the inner letters

explanation.surface: Reading a harsh review makes you privately reveal your true mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de vie, French for water of life, is a clear brandy distilled from fruit, a type of spirit.

clue.text: Nurse on flipping second warning

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it round, so the word for second runs backwards

parts.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse
MO, as in 'half a mo', is a moment or second; turned round

explanation.surface: A nurse on her shift loses her temper and issues a second warning.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'Nurse on' the other piece places it after; MO is British for a short moment.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign of what is to come, often a warning of trouble.

clue.text: Approve detective sergeant's reforms

parts.note: to say amen to something is to approve it
DS is the abbreviation for detective sergeant

explanation.surface: A chief signs off a detective sergeant's proposed changes to procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend something is to change it for the better, which is what one does when one reforms it.

clue.text: Partially unmask a terrifying iceman

indicators.note: partially means only part of the following words is used, the answer lying inside them

parts.note: letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: Someone partly reveals a frightening man made of ice, or a horror villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A skater glides on ice, so the answer is a man of the ice in a playful sense.

clue.text: Little sign of queen leaving balcony

indicators.note: leaving means departing from, so the queen's letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: a terrace is a raised platform or balcony
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: Barely a sign of the queen as she left the royal balcony.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a slight mark or indication that something was present, a little sign of it.

clue.text: Host entertains Charlie with attractive escort

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a host is an army
Charlie is the NATO code word for C
and means with or along with

explanation.surface: A party host welcomes Charlie, who arrives with a good-looking companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Arm candy is an informal term for a glamorous companion taken to events mainly to be seen with.

clue.text: Odd bits of dagger located after party trick

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the odd bits are the letters in odd-numbered positions, first, third, fifth

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A dagger turns up after a party, a sinister trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Located after' puts the dagger's letters behind those for party.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a cunning trick or ruse to avoid something.

clue.text: Visionary movement introduced by Marcus Aurelius?

parts.note: Marcus Aurelius was a Roman emperor, so what he brings in is Roman
a tic is an involuntary movement

explanation.surface: A philosophical movement founded by the Stoic emperor Marcus Aurelius.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a school of thought; movement is in fact a twitch, and the Roman is put in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic is an idealistic dreamer with grand, unrealistic visions, so a visionary.

clue.text: Scotsman going west notices divine females

indicators.note: west is to the left on a map, so in an across entry the name runs right to left

parts.note: ads are notices, advertisements
Ian is a typical Scottish name; reversed

explanation.surface: A Scotsman heading west spots some heavenly women.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiads are water nymphs in Greek myth, minor female deities of springs and rivers.

clue.text: Poor Schopenhauer lacking cash supply at this stage

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the remaining letters are put into disorder
lacking means without, so certain letters are taken out of the name

parts.note: the German philosopher's name
these four letters are removed from the name

explanation.surface: Penniless Schopenhauer runs out of money to supply his needs at this point in his life.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereupon is a formal adverb meaning immediately after this, at this point in time.

clue.text: Soprano in Germany?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano
taken as written
GER is the abbreviation for Germany

explanation.surface: An opera diva performing in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer: a soprano anywhere, Germany included, is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is the highest female voice, and the person with that voice is a vocalist.
